## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Siṅgālajātaka* (Ja 142), rendered as *The Jackal*, is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Jātaka section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded in its introductory blurb, the Buddha recounted the story while staying at the Bamboo-grove (Veḷuvana) [SuttaCentral]. The occasion arose when the monks gathered in the Hall of Truth to discuss Devadatta's plots to assassinate the Buddha. In response, the Buddha related that Devadatta had similarly sought his destruction in past lifetimes, only to bring grievous harm upon himself, and introduced the story of the past with the opening line, "Thy tightening grip" [SuttaCentral].

Neither curated parallels from SuttaCentral nor computational alignments from DharmaNexus indicate any cross-language parallels or Pali-internal text reuse for this discourse (DharmaNexus records no matches with a score ≥ 10) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral identifies four modern translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship and search dossiers, mentions of the name *Singāla* frequently refer to other texts—predominantly the *Singālovāda Sutta* (DN 31) or the distinct *Sigāla Jātaka* (Ja 113)—meaning the text itself is rarely treated individually in the matched literature.
